acceptance_criteria.criterion: Clicking "Reorder Stores" from the main table switches to the reorder sub-view.
Each store row shows label, ID, and Move Up/Move Down buttons.
First row's Move Up and last row's Move Down are disabled.
Each move sends PUT /api/stores/order with the full reordered array and re-renders.
Done button returns to the main store list with the updated order.
A priority explanation banner is visible: "Store order determines priority — when the same repository is registered in multiple stores, the first store wins."

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria were already implemented in config-stores.js from prior WP-006 work: csRenderReorderView() renders the sub-view with label+ID rows and Up/Down buttons; first/last boundary buttons are disabled; csMoveStore() calls API.reorderStores() for PUT /api/stores/order with optimistic re-render; Done button wired to csReorderMode=false + csRefreshTab(); priority explanation banner rendered inline.

Added loading-state guard: after optimistic re-render in csMoveStore(), all .cs-move-up and .cs-move-down buttons are immediately disabled for the duration of the API round-trip, preventing race conditions from rapid consecutive moves. Buttons are re-enabled naturally when the API response triggers a fresh csRenderReorderView() call.
All 3944 existing tests pass with no regressions.

comments.note: csMoveStore() re-fetches/re-renders the full reorder view on both optimistic update and API success, so contentEl is referenced by closure but re-queried would be safer. Low priority as the element is long-lived and functionally correct.

csWireEvents() in config-stores.js re-registers sync-badge hover listeners on every re-render (even in reorder mode where no sync badges exist). Could guard with an early return when csReorderMode is true, but impact is negligible.

The for-loop disabling move buttons after optimistic render (lines added in this WP) could be extracted into a small csDisableMoveBtns(contentEl) helper for readability, but one-time use doesn't justify the abstraction.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified against implementation in config-stores.js. Loading-state guard (this WP's delta) disables all move buttons immediately after optimistic re-render and re-enables on API success — race condition prevented. CSS classes confirmed present in styles.css. Full regression suite: 3944/3944 tests pass across 138 files.

comments.note: csShowTableError() silently no-ops in reorder mode because #cs-table-error only exists in the main table view; the error message from a failed API.reorderStores() call is lost before csRefreshTab() reloads the view. Not an AC requirement, but the reorder view could include its own error target element for better UX.
.cs-move-btn class listed in WP scope was replaced by .cs-move-up / .cs-move-down classes — functionally equivalent. Button styling is provided by btn btn-sm btn-secondary directly; no visual gap.

summary: WP-007 PASS. The loading-state guard in csMoveStore() is correctly implemented: optimistic re-render fires first, events are re-wired, then all .cs-move-up/.cs-move-down buttons are immediately disabled for the duration of the API round-trip. The disable occurs synchronously after csWireEvents(), so the registered click handler's !disabled guard is always respected — no race window exists. The closure over contentEl in csMoveStore() is safe because #config-tab-content persists across innerHTML replacements. The swap, order-array build, and error-path full-refresh pattern are all idiomatic with the rest of the file.

Fix-Forward applied: guarded the sync-badge hover-listener section in csWireEvents() with `if (csReorderMode) return;` — csReorderMode was already declared and maintained as module state but never read as a guard. In reorder mode no .cs-sync-badge elements exist so the loop was already a no-op; the guard makes the intent explicit and eliminates a redundant querySelectorAll call on every csMoveStore() render cycle. 3944/3944 tests pass after the change.

comments.note: csWireEvents(): added `if (csReorderMode) return;` guard before the sync-badge hover-listener loop. csReorderMode was already tracked as module state (line 21) and set correctly on enter/exit, but was never read anywhere. In reorder mode the querySelectorAll('.cs-sync-badge') always returns an empty NodeList; the guard eliminates the redundant DOM query and documents the intended use of the variable. Purely non-behavioral — confirmed by 3944/3944 test pass.

csShowTableError() silently no-ops in reorder mode because #cs-table-error is rendered only by renderStoresTab(), not csRenderReorderView(). A failed API.reorderStores() call therefore loses its error message (the catch branch calls csShowTableError() then csRefreshTab() which restores correct state, so correctness is unaffected). Future improvement: add an error target element to csRenderReorderView(), or route the error to a fallback display path before calling csRefreshTab().

[documentation-forward] csRenderReorderView() has no error target element — the module-state comment block at the top of config-stores.js should note that csShowTableError() is a no-op when csReorderMode is true, and document the fallback (csRefreshTab() restores state on API failure).

summary: Addressed the documentation-forward item from code review: updated the module-state comment block in config-stores.js to note that csShowTableError() is a no-op while csReorderMode is true, explaining why (#cs-table-error only exists in the main table view) and documenting the fallback behavior (csMoveStore() catch branch calls csRefreshTab() which restores correct view state).

Added a 'Reorder sub-view classes' section to ui-components.md section 11b, documenting all eight reorder-specific CSS classes introduced by WP-006/WP-007: .cs-reorder-view, .cs-reorder-info, .cs-reorder-row, .cs-reorder-label, .cs-reorder-btns, .cs-move-up, .cs-move-down, and .cs-move-disabled (including the loading-state disable behavior added in this WP). These classes were in styles.css but absent from the manifest documentation.

Existing README and API surface documentation required no changes — the reorder feature is a GUI-only sub-view wired to the existing PUT /api/stores/order endpoint already documented in api-surface.md.

comments.note: Documentation-forward item fully addressed: csShowTableError no-op in reorder mode is now documented in the module-state comment block, with explanation and fallback path. No active investigation of root cause was needed — the behavior is intentional and the fallback is correct.
ui-components.md section 11b was missing all eight reorder-specific CSS classes. These were added with accurate descriptions derived directly from styles.css and config-stores.js behavior.
